name: Vinack's stepson
description: A farmer and the narrator, who hated his stepfather Vinack, runs the farm after his mother's death, and lets Vinack walk to his death before the minotaurs.

timeline.summary: The narrator's mother marries Vinack when the narrator is ten, after the narrator was beaten by farmhands' sons.
timeline.quote: When I was ten when my mother married him and, at the time, I didn't hate him.

timeline.summary: The narrator confronts Vinack after seeing his mother's bruised face, and Vinack strikes him.
timeline.quote: He told me to know my place and struck me in the head.

timeline.summary: The narrator tells Vinack he is a selfish beast, and Vinack beats him until the mother and farmhands throw him out.
The narrator's mother dies of failing health when he is seventeen, leaving him in charge of the farmland.
timeline.quote: My mother passed away when I was seventeen and I was then in charge of our farmland.

timeline.summary: Vinack returns after ten years asking for help against the minotaurs, and the narrator strikes him.
timeline.quote: I would not have struck him if he hadn't said, "I need your help, Son."

timeline.summary: The narrator agrees to help and Vinack proposes striking down the minotaur oracle.
timeline.quote: Vinack's plan was to go into their territory and strike down their oracle.

timeline.summary: The narrator searches Zerili's home and ledger and concludes that the village secretly pays human tribute and that Vinack means him to die.
timeline.quote: Vinack meant for me to die.

timeline.summary: At the minotaur camp the narrator presses a dagger to Vinack's back, and Vinack reveals the sacrifice will be himself.
timeline.quote: "No, Son," he said, shaking his head. "The sacrifice will be me."

timeline.summary: Vinack offers himself as sacrifice to the oracle, who crushes and snaps his body, and a blood mist fills the minotaurs while the narrator thinks he sees Mogis.
timeline.quote: Without ceremony, the shaman slammed his fist downwards on Vinack's head, pushing it down into his body.

timeline.summary: The narrator returns to the village praised as the hero who stopped the minotaur menace, and concludes he hates himself.
timeline.quote: I let that man walk to his death.

relations.quote: I know you hate me. I know I wronged you and your mother.

pages_say.description: A farmer and the narrator, who hated his stepfather Vinack, runs the farm after his mother's death, and lets Vinack walk to his death before the minotaurs.
